Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today's call

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned: 

- Summary: FinPay is evaluating an in-production LLM path for real-time fraud scoring in the payments flow. Main constraint is predictable low latency for single-request completions and sustained throughput during peak traffic windows.
- Requirements you called out: p95 latency target ~150-200ms for a typical 300-token completion, sustained ~150 requests/sec during peak, and spikes to ~300 req/sec for short windows.
- Data posture: you confirmed no PHI, but payments data with PCI considerations; you'll need VPC connectivity and audit logs for reviewers.
- Open questions: whether Hosted API can meet latency SLOs or if Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is required for determinism.

Next steps: 
1) I'll follow up with product/infra to validate how Hosted performs at your target latency/throughput and share benchmark numbers (p50/p95/p99) and trade-offs.
2) Marissa to share pricing/contract options for Dedicated vs Hosted once we confirm numbers.
3) Rajesh / procurement to share calendar availability for procurement discussion next week.

I'll loop Neha on the perf details. Thanks again — talk soon.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@finpay.com>

Date: 2027-08-13T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today's call

Thanks Dylan — good summary. A couple clarifications from my side: 

- The 150-200ms target is p95 for end-to-end inference time (model server + networking). We can tolerate a handful of p99s during spikes but p95 is the gating metric for product launch.
- Typical request size is ~250-400 tokens; average 320 tokens.
- Sustained: target 120-180 req/sec during business hours; peak bursts up to 300 req/sec for up to 10 minutes.
- Throughput: during batch QA jobs we may also run higher token/sec workloads but those can be scheduled off-peak.
- Security: VPC peering is required. SOC2 reports requested later in the procurement packet.

As for deployment preference, our platform team leans toward Dedicated if it guarantees the latency/throughput without throttling or noisy-neighbor issues. If Hosted can demonstrate consistent p95 <200ms at our profile, we could consider it for faster onboarding.

Procurement: procurement@finpay.com is copied for timeline planning — target decision by end of month if the numbers check out.

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay

From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted vs Dedicated - FinPay requirements

Thanks for the ping — quick technical readout below. Attaching a short benchmark CSV and our standard Dedicated SLA PDF that covers isolation and capacity guarantees.

Summary: 
- Hosted API: For a 320-token average completion on our verified 13B model (quantized), typical p95 observed in our hosted fleet is ~220-300ms in the us-west region under normal load. P99 can spike significantly during noisy-neighbor events unless you buy a higher priority tier. We can run a targeted Hosted validation with FinPay's sample traffic to see real numbers.

- Dedicated: A reserved GPU pool (H100 or A100 cluster depending on model) provides deterministic performance. Our internal Dedicated runs for similar profiles show p95 around 120-160ms for 320-token completions on an H100-backed deployment with optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for single-request low-latency mode. Throughput: a properly sized Dedicated pool can sustain 200+ req/sec with headroom for the 300 req/sec bursts, and autoscaling/burst configs can cover short spikes.

Trade-offs: 
- Hosted: faster onboarding, pay-as-you-go, but latency not guaranteed at the p95 <200ms target unless we move to a premium isolation tier (higher cost) or run a dedicated Hosted lane for you.
- Dedicated: higher committed cost but provides predictable latency/throughput, VPC connectivity, and stronger audit/log guarantees (suitable for procurement).

Recommendation: Given FinPay's p95 target and burst profile, Dedicated is the conservative choice to meet launch SLOs. We should still offer a short Hosted validation test so they can compare actual numbers with their payload.

Next steps I can take: 
1) Run a 48-hour Hosted validation using FinPay's sample traffic (need sample payloads and an API key scoped to the test).
2) If validation shows Hosted meets p95 <200ms with acceptable p99, propose Hosted pilot pricing; otherwise prepare Dedicated sizing + draft SOW.
3) Share Dedicated sizing estimate and SLA doc (attached).

Attachments: latency-benchmarks.csv, redwood-dedicated-sla.pdf

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Applied ML / Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
